titulo: Stable × draft: reading the spec, Chrome Status, and the browsers' positions, with dates
lead: WebMCP has already changed its name once and may change again before the origin trial ends. Whoever teaches or implements it needs to know, with dates, what the spec says, which browser runs it, and who is against it. In this lesson you read all of that straight from the primary sources with a script, and you learn to separate what is foundation from what is lab work.
objetivo: read from the source, with dates, where WebMCP stands: spec, origin trial, and each browser's position.

secoes.titulo: What is foundation and what is lab work on 10/19/2026

nos.detalhe: Semantic, accessible HTML, a labeled form, MCP on the server (2026-07-28 revision), good tool design. Can be the basis for exercises, assessment, and production.
WebMCP: Draft Community Group Report from 10/16/2026, from the Web Machine Learning Community Group. The document itself says: "not a W3C Standard nor is it on the W3C Standards Track".
Chrome Status: "Proposed", dev trial since 146, origin trial from 149 to 156, no stable release date. For local development, use the enable-webmcp-testing flag. Edge: origin trial in 150.
Mozilla: neutral position (08/03/2026). WebKit (Safari): against, with objections on API design, privacy, security, and portability. Don't promise it will work in every browser.

secoes.legenda: Exercises and assessment on the stable foundation. WebMCP as a lab, with a date and feature detection.

secoes.titulo: Where to look and what to look for

texto: At the top of webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp: the document type and the date. If the date has changed since your last read, reread what you use.
Look for the name of the surface. On 10/16/2026 it is document.modelContext; navigator.modelContext no longer appears.
The implementation-status.md in the spec repository says where there is an origin trial (Chrome 149, Edge 150) and what else exists (Brave Leo experimental, ChatGPT Desktop).
Chrome Status (entry 5117755740913664) gives the trial range and the stage.
Mozilla and WebKit publish positions in open issues: mozilla/standards-positions #1412 and WebKit/standards-positions #670. The "position:" label gives the position.
Everything that depends on a flag, origin trial, or explainer gets the "experimental on DD/MM/YYYY" stamp. WebMCP is preparation, not ranking: visibility in AI is a topic for the inemaSEO Program.

exemplo.rot: A real case of an API that changed
exemplo.texto: The switch from navigator.modelContext to document.modelContext was accepted on 05/19/2026 (PR #177). Courses written before that date teach the old API.

secoes.titulo: The state of WebMCP, read from the sources
secoes.sub: estado.sh downloads the spec and implementation-status.md, and reads the two position issues through the public GitHub API, with no login and no key. All you need is curl.

abas.rot: Common mistake: copying the date from a post
abas.html: Material from before May 2026 still shows navigator.modelContext, and September courses cite the 09/17/2026 draft. The date that counts is the one in the spec header on the day you read it. If the estado.sh shows a date other than 10/16/2026, the spec changed after this course: reread it before using any example from here.

perguntas.p: What is the status of the WebMCP document on 10/16/2026?
opcoes: A W3C Recommendation, already a web standard
A Community Group draft, outside the standards track
A Chrome standard, implemented in all browsers
An approved IETF specification, already an RFC
perguntas.explica: The document itself says "not a W3C Standard nor is it on the W3C Standards Track". Teaching it as a standard is a mistake.

perguntas.p: What is WebKit's (Safari's) position on WebMCP?
opcoes: In favor, with an implementation planned
perguntas.explica: WebKit issue #670 has the label position: oppose. Neutral is Mozilla's.

perguntas.p: In Chrome, how is WebMCP available to your site's visitors today?
opcoes: With the site's origin trial token (Chrome 149–156)
In every stable Chrome, with nothing for the site to do
Only by installing an official Google extension in Chrome
Only in Chrome for Android, with the flag turned on
perguntas.explica: Origin trial from 149 to 156, with a token per origin. The enable-webmcp-testing flag is for developing on your own machine, not for visitors.

perguntas.p: estado.sh shows a spec date other than 10/16/2026. What should you do?
opcoes: Nothing: spec dates don't change the published API
Turn WebMCP off on the site until the standard is released
Reread the spec before using the examples
Swap document for navigator in the code
perguntas.explica: The API has already changed its name once. A new date calls for a reread; going back to navigator would mean going back to the old version.
